entry.title: OPC Weekly Report: One-Person Companies Powered by AI — June 2026 W26
entry.content:
Week 26 (June 22 – 27, 2026) — The biggest news this week: Seede AI, a one-person company from Chengdu, closed a million-dollar seed round — 300,000 registered users, 10,000+ paying customers, built by a solo founder under 30 using an OPC model. This is no longer a concept; it’s commercial reality.

Meanwhile, Guangzhou’s Haizhu district unleashed its strongest OPC incentive yet — up to ¥5 million per project — and Jinan’s OPC community surpassed 400 resident companies. AI Agents have moved from “usable” to “reliable,” and one-person companies are transitioning from water-cooler talk to a mainstream entrepreneurial force. Here’s your full roundup.

🏛️ Policy Watch: Cities Go All-In on OPC Talent

Guangzhou Haizhu: Record ¥5M Incentive

Haizhu district released its AI OPC innovation development measures, offering up to ¥5 million in single-project support covering startup capital, R&D subsidies, and computing vouchers. This is the most aggressive OPC policy seen to date.

Jinan: 407 OPC Companies Onboarded

Jinan’s “Spring Computing Token Factory” has integrated 21 computing centers with peta-scale heterogeneous computing power. Signed OPC companies enjoy 50% computing cost reductions, with top-tier projects getting an additional 30% long-term discount — capped at ¥100K annual subsidy.

Chongqing: “Future Star” 10-Point OPC Plan

Chongqing launched a dedicated OPC portal on its “YuQi Online” platform featuring AI-powered name suggestions, business scope packages, and automated document generation. “One address, multiple companies” thresholds have been relaxed, and entrepreneurial parks no longer require property certificates for registration.

Suzhou Wujiang: ¥2B AI Fund + ¥10B Credit Line

Suzhou Wujiang deployed a ¥2 billion AI direct investment fund and ¥10 billion dedicated credit line. Free OpenClaw-style Agent deployment services are provided, along with ¥1,500/month rental subsidies for up to 3 years.

Yongzhou: 3-Year Rent-Free + ¥4M Startup Loans

OPC policy has cascaded from tier-1 cities to tier-3/4 cities. Yongzhou offers 3-year rent-free office space and up to ¥4 million in startup loans — making it increasingly affordable to launch a one-person company anywhere in China.

Bottom line: Cities are no longer just talking about OPC support — they’re writing checks. From computing subsidies to free office space, the cost barrier for one-person companies has been essentially eliminated. The question now: are you getting on the table?

🔥 Success Stories: OPC in Action

🏆 Headliner: Seede AI Raises Million-Dollar Seed Round

Founder: Long Yi | Location: Chengdu
Product: AI visual design tool with proprietary rendering engine
Key Metrics: 300K registered users, 10K+ paying customers, $1M+ seed round

Long Yi launched Seede AI as a true OPC — one person handling R&D, operations, and GTM. His approach broke from mainstream text-to-image models, solving AI design’s “text corruption, non-editable output, aesthetic homogeneity” pain points. Targeting e-commerce, SMBs, and knowledge workers, Seede delivers PPT, poster, and infographic creation. He’s since grown to a small remote team, but the MVP and first wave of customers came from one person alone.

AI Video: From Programmer to Overlanding Content Creator

A former software engineer pivoted to an AI-driven travel video editing niche as an OPC, taking his product to the Chengdu-Chongqing OPC investment roadshow stage. Covered by China Business Journal, his story exemplifies how “a technical person armed with AI goes further.”

Corporate Adoption: Dreame Tech Incubates 200+ OPC Units

Dreame Technology (a major consumer electronics company) adopted an internal OPC model, incubating 200+ business units with an average setup time of just 12 days. The model proves that one-person squads can deliver team-level output — even inside large enterprises.

Cross-Border Live Commerce: 6-Figure Monthly Revenue in 4 Months

Humi Tech founder Chen Zishun achieved six-figure monthly revenue within 4 months as a solo operator using AI tools + livestream commerce. Cross-border e-commerce, AI tool development, and vertical knowledge services are emerging as OPC “golden sectors.”

📊 Industry Trends: AI Agent Hits Mass Adoption Inflection Point

The Numbers That Matter

Enterprise AI Agent adoption50%+Up from 18% in 2024

5 Core AI Agent Trends for 2026

  1. Multi-Agent Collaboration — Specialized Agent networks replacing monolithic models
  2. MCP Protocol Bridges Data Silos — Standardized Model Context Protocol connects Agents to enterprise systems
  3. Production-Ready Agents — Moving from POC to full production deployment
  4. Open-Source Tool Chain Explosion — OpenClaw, Dify, LingtiStudio accelerate OPC viability
  5. Ultra-Long Context Windows — AI now handles full-project analysis, not just Q&A

🛠️ The OPC Toolkit: 2026 Arsenal

AI Agent Platforms

  • OpenClaw — OS/app automation workflow platform
  • Dify — LLM app orchestration, ideal for SaaS/AI products
  • Bika.ai — OPC-dedicated AI organizer with multi-Agent chat
  • LingtiStudio — End-to-end AI video production Agent

  • Cursor — #1 AI coding environment among developers
  • GitHub Copilot — Handles 80% of code writing and debugging
  • UXbot — Full-cycle: planning → UI generation → multi-platform code
  • Replit Agent — Browser-based: description to deployment

AI Content Creation

  • Lovable — Natural language → fully functional web apps
  • Midjourney / Stable Diffusion — Marketing assets and UI design

💡 Founder Insights: Lao Qin’s Take

“The bottleneck for OPC isn’t technology — it’s customer acquisition.”

AI makes product launch easy, but the first customer remains the hardest part. When 60-point capabilities are available to everyone, your Go-to-Market efficiency determines your ceiling.

“Your company’s limit is the strength of your system, not your individual ability.”

Alibaba Cloud’s WAVES data shows that traditional “coding developers” now make up only 20% of cloud platform users — product/ops people account for 35%, business owners 21%. Infrastructure is evolving from “for tech geeks” to “for people with ideas.”

“The monetization shift: sell systems, not time.”

Freelancers sell time. OPCs sell systems that compound. Three proven paths: (1) lease AI digital workers to SMBs on monthly subscriptions, (2) become AI transformation consultants for traditional enterprises, (3) build personal-IP Agents that monetize knowledge and traffic.

entry.title: The Rise of OPC: How One-Person Companies Are Eating Traditional Organizations in the AI Era
entry.content:
The Rise of OPC: How One-Person Companies Are Eating Traditional Organizations in the AI Era

2026 Week 26 OPC Entrepreneurship Trend Deep Dive Report

📌 Core Insight: In 2026, OPC (One-Person Company) has transformed from concept to reality. AI tools have made “one person army” possible: past SaaS companies requiring 5-10 person teams can now be operated solo with AI Agents, completing the full chain from product development to marketing and customer service. This is not just efficiency improvement—it’s a fundamental reshaping of business organization.

Table of Contents

  1. What is OPC? Why Now?
  2. Policy Dividends: 20+ Cities Racing into the OPC Track
  3. 2026 OPC Golden Tool Stack: The “Digital Departments” of a One-Person Company
  4. Real Cases: OPC Is Not Just Theory
  5. The Evolution of OPC Communities: From Office Space to Ecosystem Collaboration
  6. Challenges and Risks: OPC Is Not a Panacea
  7. Future Outlook: 2026 Second Half OPC Trend Predictions
  8. Conclusion: OPC Is Evolution, Not Regression

1. What is OPC? Why Now? {#what-is-opc}

1.1 Core Definition of OPC

OPC (One-Person Company) refers to individual entrepreneurs who leverage AI capabilities to independently complete the full-cycle business loop—from product conception and design to R&D and marketing—starting a business in a “one-person-supports-a-whole-team” mode.

🧬 The Core Logic of OPC:

Carbon-Based Wisdom (Human) + Silicon-Based Execution (AI) = Complete Company

  • Human does decision/creativity/strategy: Define boundaries, orchestrate logic, judge value
  • AI does execution/standardization/processes: Code generation, content creation, data analysis, customer service

1.2 Why OPC Exploded in 2026

💡 The Turning Point: The collective upgrade of Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities in 2025 enabled people with zero coding knowledge to independently complete entire project R&D. This is the real reason OPC exploded in 2026.

Three Core Drivers:

  1. AI Tool Maturity (2024-2026): Evolution from “code completion” to “Intent-Driven” systematic development
  2. Threshold Completely Shattered: Past SaaS products requiring 5-person teams (frontend, backend, UI, testing, product) can now be completed by one person with AI toolchains in 48 hours from project initiation to launch
  3. Cost Reduced to 1%: Numerous solo entrepreneurship projects have emerged in Silicon Valley, with R&D cycles compressed from months to days, and costs reduced to 1% of traditional teams

2. Policy Dividends: 20+ Cities Racing into the OPC Track {#policy-dividends}

In 2026, OPC has upgraded from folk experiment to policy-supported entrepreneurship model. According to the China OPC Development Research Report 2026, domestic OPC development is surging:

🏙️ Geographic Distribution

Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, and emerging industrial cities in central and western regions

👥 Demographic Characteristics

Founding main force concentrated in Post-90s and Post-00s generations

💼 Industry Characteristics

Light assets, high intelligence, new business formats

📊 Market Size

Expected to exceed 800 billion yuan

2.1 Hainan Free Trade Port: OPC Policy Testbed

On June 20, 2026, four departments of Hainan Province jointly issued the Artificial Intelligence OPC One-Person Company Special Support Policy, creating an AI-enabled “super individual” entrepreneurship ecosystem.

🎁 Core Policy Dividends:

  • Tax Incentives: Corporate income tax 15%, personal income tax 15% (dual 15% incentive)
  • Limited Liability Protection: 100% holding by one person, no need for partners, zero decision-making friction
  • Free Office Space: OPC communities provide rent-free, move-in-ready workstations
  • Computing Power Subsidies: Quality communities can receive up to 8 million yuan in provincial-level rewards
  • Fully Online Registration: Fastest 1-day certificate issuance, no physical venue required

2.2 WAIC OPC Independent Pioneer Challenge

In 2026, WAIC (World Artificial Intelligence Conference) partnered with OpenCSG to launch the OPC Independent Pioneer Challenge, becoming the world’s first top-tier incubation platform specifically designed for super individuals and AI entrepreneurs. This is not just a competition—it’s a complete ecosystem for discovering potential, linking resources, and nurturing future unicorns.

3. 2026 OPC Golden Tool Stack: The “Digital Departments” of a One-Person Company {#tool-stack}

To support an OPC business generating millions in annual revenue, you need a set of “tool matrices” that can automatically flow. Here are the most recommended OPC technology stacks for 2026:

RoleCore Tools (2026 Recommended)Core Output
Product/UI Designv0.dev / LovableInteractive prototypes and React style code
Full-Stack DevelopmentCursor / Devin / TRAEFull-stack code generation and automatic refactoring
Logic Brain (Multi-Agent)LangGraph / OpenClawComplex state machine Agent orchestration
Marketing Content豆豆羊 / JasperAutomatic content generation, layout, and publishing
Customer ServiceIntercom / AI Chatbot7×24 intelligent customer service
Data AnalysisJulius / ViktorAutomated reports and data insights

⚠️ Important Reminder: The key to success in 2026 is NOT “how many AI tools you can use,” but “how many AI Agents you can orchestrate.” Your core competitiveness lies in the efficiency of calling AI resources, not the number of lines of code you write.

4. Real Cases: OPC Is Not Just Theory {#real-cases}

4.1 Typical Case: Li Jiehui

Li Jiehui is a typical representative of the OPC model. He independently completed product development from 0 to 1 using AI tools and achieved profitability in a short time. This case proves: OPC is not about “one person carrying all the work,” but about “one person learning to design task flows, then using AI Agents, automation tools, and external service networks to run tasks.”

4.2 Optics Valley of China OPC Entrepreneurship Ecosystem

Wuhan’s Optics Valley is becoming a new hot spot for OPC entrepreneurship. The “One-Person Company” (OPC) new entrepreneurship model is thriving in Optics Valley, thanks to the rapid evolution of AI technology.

4.3 Indie Hacker Practice: Launch SaaS in 48 Hours

In 2026, the threshold for indie hackers has been completely shattered. Past SaaS products requiring 5-person teams can now be completed by one person in 48 hours from project initiation to launch through AI toolchains.

📊 Efficiency Formula (2026 Version):

  • I (Idea): Your product creativity and logic loop closure
  • A (AI Leverage): Your ability to control AI tools (Prompt precision, toolchain integration)
  • n (Collaboration Coefficient): When using Multi-Agent collaboration, n increases exponentially
  • C (Complexity): Complexity under traditional development models (diminishing through AI)

5. The Evolution of OPC Communities: From Office Space to Ecosystem Collaboration {#opc-communities}

In 2026, OPC communities are gradually evolving from simple office spaces or entrepreneurship groups to new organizational carriers connecting AI tools, individual entrepreneurs, industrial resources, and enterprise application scenarios.

5.1 Core Value of OPC Communities

  • Not “one person isolated entrepreneurship”: But allowing individuals to collaborate within an ecosystem
  • Resource Sharing: Computing power subsidies, office space, legal services, financing connections
  • Complementary Capabilities: OPC entrepreneurs in different fields can outsource tasks to each other
  • Brand Endorsement: Joining a quality OPC community equals gaining credit enhancement

5.2 Hainan OPC Community Plan

  • 2026 Goal: Pioneer 3 quality communities
  • 2028 Goal: Cumulatively cultivate 10+ quality communities, incubate 100+ quality OPC enterprises, gather 1000+ innovative talents
  • Spatial Layout: “One core, two poles, multi-point linkage” (Haikou as core, Chengmai and Sanya as bidirectional supports, other cities with differentiated development)

6. Challenges and Risks: OPC Is Not a Panacea {#challenges}

🚫 What I DON’T Favor: OPC where “one person does everything”

I favor OPC (One-Person Company), but I do NOT favor OPC where “one person stubbornly carries product, R&D, sales, customer service, operations, and delivery.” The truly valuable OPC discussion in 2026 centers on:

  1. One person learning to design task flows
  2. Then using AI Agents, automation tools, and external service networks to run tasks
  3. Letting AI undertake standardized, repetitive work

6.1 Scenarios Suitable for OPC

  • ✅ SaaS product development and operations
  • ✅ Content creation and knowledge monetization
  • ✅ Vertical domain consulting services
  • ✅ Cross-border e-commerce independent sites
  • ✅ AI tool integration and customization

6.2 Scenarios NOT Suitable for OPC

  • ❌ Services requiring large amounts of offline manual delivery
  • ❌ Manufacturing requiring heavy asset investment
  • ❌ Ventures requiring complex supply chain management
  • ❌ Core businesses in strongly regulated industries (e.g., finance, healthcare)

6.3 How Can Ordinary People Catch the OPC Dividend?

  1. Find a niche track: Don’t aim to build “the next OpenAI” right away—find a segmented problem you can solve
  2. Learn to orchestrate AI: In 2026, AI tools are not lacking; what’s lacking are people who know how to use them
  3. Build personal brand: Your core asset in OPC is your personal brand and trustworthiness
  4. Leverage policy dividends: Hainan, Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta all have OPC special support policies
  5. Join OPC communities: Don’t entrepreneurship alone—find your “digital colleague” network

7. Future Outlook: 2026 Second Half OPC Trend Predictions {#future-outlook}

🔮 Key Trends for H2 2026:

  1. Multi-Agent collaboration becomes mainstream: Evolution from single AI tool usage to multi-agent collaborative workflows
  2. OPC specialized division of labor: “OPC service providers” will emerge (e.g., OPC legal, OPC finance, OPC marketing)
  3. Passive income普及 (Popularization of passive income): Achieving “sleep income” models through AI automation
  4. OPC integration with traditional enterprises: Traditional enterprises begin purchasing OPC AI solutions
  5. Continued policy support escalation: More cities are expected to introduce OPC special support policies

8. Conclusion: OPC Is Evolution, Not Regression {#conclusion}

OPC (One-Person Company) is NOT “regressing to individual entrepreneurship,” but rather a major evolution of business organization forms in the AI era. It reconstructs the organizational model of traditional entrepreneurship, with the core essence being “single-person led, AI implemented.”

AI undertakes all standardized, repetitive work, while entrepreneurs focus on core decision-making, innovation breakthroughs, and value judgment—this is the essence of OPC, and the new paradigm that every entrepreneur in 2026 needs to deeply understand.

🎯 Action Recommendations

If you are seriously considering OPC entrepreneurship, now is the best time. But please remember:

  • OPC is NOT “one person stubbornly carrying everything,” but “one person + AI team”
  • In 2026, what matters is NOT how much AI technology you know, but whether you know how to leverage AI’s power
  • Find a small niche, hand over miscellaneous tasks like writing, formatting, and publishing to AI, and interface with clients yourself
  • Time investment is worth it: Learning to use Cursor, LangGraph, v0.dev will exponentially increase your productivity

References and Further Reading

  • China OPC Development Research Report 2026
  • WAIC OPC Independent Pioneer Challenge Official Website
  • Hainan AI OPC One-Person Company Special Support Policy (2026)
  • Optics Valley of China OPC Entrepreneurship Ecosystem White Paper

entry.title: AI Agents at Tipping Point: Your OPC Startup Playbook — W26a Report
entry.content:
Week 26 (June 2026) — The data is in, and it’s unambiguous: we’ve crossed the AI Agent adoption chasm. Enterprise AI Agent adoption hit 50%+ (up from 18% in 2024), the global enterprise Agent market topped $18 billion, and 66% of enterprises have deployed customer service AI agents — with 77% of those reporting positive ROI within 60 days.

For OPC founders, this isn’t just a statistic — it’s the infrastructure layer that makes one-person companies viable at scale. Here’s the full picture.

📊 This Week’s Core Data

MetricValueSignal
Solo-founded startups as share of new companies1 in 3OPC is now statistically mainstream
Solo-founder growth over 6 years+53%Accelerating, not decelerating
Enterprise AI Agent adoption50%+Up from 18% in 2024
Enterprise Agent market size (2026)$18BInstitutional validation
Customer service Agent adoption66%Highest vertical penetration
Enterprises seeing 60-day ROI77%Business case is proven
OPC efficiency vs. traditional team8-10xStructural advantage, not hype
OPC minimum startup cost<¥4,000Barrier to entry is gone

🔥 Top Stories This Week

🏢 VCs Are Betting on One-Person Teams

Venture capital firms began actively investing in AI-powered micro-startup teams in late 2025 — many with just 1-3 people and monthly burn under ¥20,000. These teams deliver what used to require 10-person groups. The investment thesis: AI collapses the team-size-to-output curve. One person handling product selection, operations, design, and customer support simultaneously is now normal.

🏛️ OPC Independent Pioneer Challenge Full Breakdown

Sam Altman’s prediction — “In the AI era, one person can build a billion-dollar unicorn” — is being cited as a founding thesis for WAIC’s OPC track. The June data confirms: the “carbon-based + silicon-based = complete company” formula now operates at commercial scale.

🤖 Enterprise AI Agents Cross the Chasm

Forty percent of enterprise applications now embed or plan to embed AI agents. Use cases have expanded from simple customer service Q&A to complex workflows: procurement, risk control, financial approvals, document processing. AI is transitioning from “co-pilot” to “employee.”

📊 66% of Enterprises Deploy Customer Service AI Agents

Salesforce survey data shows customer service AI Agent deployment jumped from 39% in 2025 to 66% in 2026. Of those, 77% allow seamless human handoff at any point — addressing the trust gap that previously blocked adoption.

🇨🇳 OPC China Framework: The Definitive Model

The OPC China community published a definitive analysis of the new organizational form: “OPC is not one person fighting alone. It’s one person orchestrating AI models, agents, automation tools, and collaborative networks to complete content, marketing, sales, and delivery in a closed business loop.” The OPC = “AI Agent + Personal Capability” organizational structure.

💡 Three Trends Reshaping OPC

📈 Trend 1: Policy Window Wide Open

Shenzhen’s systematic OPC city-level plan offers training computing vouchers, model vouchers, and data vouchers. Suzhou’s top projects get ¥1M in startup funding with a target of 30+ OPC communities by 2028. Cities are competing, not just participating.

🔧 Trend 2: AI Tool Stack Reaches Maturity

Products like Tycoon AI and Paperclip (open-source “AI board of directors”) let solo founders manage 1,000 AI agents running in parallel, 24/7. Critical technical breakthroughs — heartbeat mechanisms, budget controls, persistent storage — make autonomous operation controllable and predictable.

💰 Trend 3: Monetization Paths Diversify

PathRevenue RangeSuitability
AI Agent deployment¥30-100K/yearTechnical founders
AI content studio¥20-50K/monthCreators & writers
AI + local services¥50-150K/yearOffline integration
AI skills training¥30-80K/yearEducators & consultants
AI vertical tools¥200K-1M+/yearDomain experts

🛠️ The OPC Core Tool Stack (June 2026)

Agent Management & Orchestration

  • Tycoon AI — AI CEO system, manages 1,000 agents
  • Paperclip — Open-source “AI board,” heartbeat + budget control
  • Kouzi / Dify / Coze — Low-code Agent development, zero-code entry
  • Accio Work — Cross-border e-commerce automation, 48-platform store creation

AI Development

  • Cursor + GitHub Copilot — 5-10x development efficiency
  • Shizai Agent — Cross-system integration, breaking data silos

Where Not to Play

“Don’t build general-purpose assistants.” The giant players already own this — compute, data, and ecosystem barriers are insurmountable. Focus on verticals that need “industry know-how + non-standard data processing.”

💵 Six Monetization Paths (Ranked)

  1. AI Agent Deployment Services — Build customer service agents, sales assistants, content generators for SMBs. Per-project: ¥5K-50K. 2-3 projects/month is achievable.

  2. Vertical Agent Product Subscriptions — Build e-commerce customer service agents or content helper agents. Monthly subscription = true passive income.

  3. Content Entrepreneurship Automation — Use agents for topic sourcing, writing, editing, publishing across platforms. Efficiency improvement: 5x+.

  4. AI Skills Training & Consulting — Demand is red-hot. Training income is stable and recurring.

  5. AI + Local Services — Combine offline resources with AI to expand service range and efficiency.

  6. AI Vertical Tool Development — Highest revenue ceiling. Target specific industry pain points with deep tools.

⚠️ Risk & Pitfall Guide

Engineering Traps

  • Don’t build general assistants — The giants already win on compute, data, and ecosystem
  • Focus on vertical niches — Choose domains needing “industry know-how + non-standard data”
  • Avoid tech stack sprawl — Your advantage is agility and low delivery cost, not engineering scale
  • Watch API costs — Set token budgets. AI dead loops can generate astronomical bills

Compliance Essentials

  • Annual audits required for OPC entities — Prove company and personal assets aren’t mixed
  • Human handoff mechanism required — Customer trust depends on it
  • Data security and API key management — These are baseline requirements, not optional

The Founders’ Contradiction

The hardest part of OPC isn’t building the product — it’s finding customers. When 60-point AI capabilities are available to everyone, your go-to-market efficiency is what separates you from the noise.

🌍 Global Pulse

  • OPC Community — Global AI-era solo founder community went live, offering resource matching and best practice sharing
  • Africa — AI tools are empowering African solopreneurs to run lightweight operations on 10-hour work weeks
  • US Trend — “Solopreneur AI Agency” is the hottest startup category in 2026, with one-person AI agencies rising fast

✅ Your Action Plan for This Week

  1. Pick a vertical — Start with an industry you already understand. Avoid generic horizontal plays
  2. Build your MVP — Use Kouzi/Dify/Coze (low-code). Don’t try to build from scratch. Perfection is the enemy
  3. Establish your audience — Tech isn’t the barrier anymore. Distribution and trust are. Start building your personal brand NOW
  4. Apply for policy benefits — Shenzhen and Suzhou are literally giving away startup money. Fill out the forms
  5. Control your burn — Target ¥20K/month or less. Get to breakeven fast. Cash is oxygen

🧠 Lao Qin’s Take

“2026 is the year AI Agents stopped being ‘interesting’ and started being ‘profitable.’”

Two things changed this month:

  1. The ROI data arrived. 77% of enterprises seeing 60-day payback on Agent deployments? That kills the “AI is just hype” argument.
  2. The infrastructure became invisible. You don’t need to think about model inference, token streaming, or agent orchestration anymore. The tools handle it. You just need to apply them.

The OPC founder’s challenge has shifted from “Can I build this?” to “Can I sell this?” That’s a much better problem to have.

⚠️ Bottom line: Pick your vertical this week. Build your MVP this month. Get your first customer before July. The window won’t stay open forever — but right now, it’s wide open.

The World AI Conference and OpenCSG launched the first-ever dedicated OPC startup competition — the strongest signal yet that the establishment is taking one-person companies seriously. Finals at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai’s Expo Center.

5. Guangdong’s Landmark OPC Action Plan

The “Supporting AI OPC Innovation Development Action Plan (2026-2028)” sets targets of 100 communities, 1,000 benchmark enterprises — backed with computing subsidies, cross-border expansion support, and full ecosystem enablement.

6. Suzhou’s “Lobster Service Zone” for OPC

Suzhou Wujiang created a dedicated OPC zone offering free Agent deployment services, a ¥2B AI direct fund, ¥10B dedicated credit line, and ¥1,500/month rental subsidies for up to 3 years. The “lobster” metaphor (AI digital employees) is now official government language.

7. Shenzhen: City-Level OPC Leadership Plan

Shenzhen’s plan targets 10+ OPC communities, 1,000+ high-growth startups, and 10,000+ AI talents by end of 2027 — backed with computing vouchers up to ¥10M.

8. Microsoft’s “OPE” Concept Goes Mainstream

Dr. Zhang Qi, Microsoft AI Asia Pacific President, introduced OPE (One-Person Enterprise) — the idea that with generative AI, an individual becomes a “minimum innovation system” capable of orchestrating tools, systems, and global resources. Beijing University Press published a book on the theme: “One person with AI can now do what used to take an entire team.”

9. Zhima Enterprise Credit Launches OPC Toolbox

Ant Group’s Zhima Enterprise Credit platform released a dedicated OPC toolkit integrating AI business opportunity matching, credit building, and cost optimization. The platform has onboarded nearly 5.7M one-person companies so far.

10. TRAE Becomes Top AI-Native IDE for Chinese Developers

Q2 2026 benchmarks show TRAE achieving 98% code generation accuracy in Chinese-language scenarios — leading among AI-native IDEs. Cumulative registered users surpassed 6M by end of 2025.

💡 What is OPC, Really?

The Core Definition

OPC (One-Person Company) is a new entrepreneurial form where a single individual, powered by AI technology, independently completes the full business loop — product design, development, operations, customer service — all without a traditional team.

The formula: Carbon-based intelligence (human) + Silicon-based execution (AI) = A complete company.

The Five Defining Characteristics

CharacteristicWhat It Means
Digital NativeBuilt on digital infrastructure and AI tools from day one — no physical office needed
Multi-Role CapabilityAI tool chain enables one person to function as PM, developer, operator, marketer, and support
10x EfficiencyAI handles repetitive/standardized work; founder focuses on strategy and creative decisions
Ecosystem-DependentDeep reliance on AI tools, cloud platforms, API economy, and external infrastructure
Scenario-DrivenProducts built around specific niches, with rapid iteration and precision positioning

The Three OPC Models

  1. Innovation Model — Disrupt traditional workflows with AI. Example: AI-driven personalized education, smart customer service outsourcing
  2. Scenario Application Model — Build targeted AI solutions for vertical pain points. Example: AI brand visibility detection
  3. Ecosystem Service Model — Provide tools, computing, or training to other OPCs. Example: AI agent deployment services

The Monetization Escalator

Stage 1 — Project Services: Use AI tools to take on outsourcing projects, validate demand, build experience
Stage 2 — Productized Services: Package proven approaches into standardized products (SaaS tools, courses, templates)
Stage 3 — Platform Play: Build a two-sided marketplace matching supply and demand — passive income, true scale

🛠️ The 2026 OPC Arsenal: 10 AI Employees + 36 Tools

Here’s the modern OPC “org chart” — a single person backed by a virtual team of AI specialists:

RoleToolsRating
🎯 Chief Strategy OfficerNotion, Perplexity, NotebookLM⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
✍️ Chief Content OfficerChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
🎨 Chief ArtistMidjourney, Jimeng AI⭐⭐⭐⭐
🖼️ Visual DesignerFigma, Canva⭐⭐⭐⭐
🎬 Video ProducerRunway ML, Jimeng AI⭐⭐⭐⭐
💻 CTOTRAE, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
📊 Data AnalystMicrosoft Copilot, Simple AI⭐⭐⭐⭐
📧 Customer Success ManagerChatGPT, automated CRM⭐⭐⭐⭐
📱 Social Media ManagerSimple AI, Kouzi (Coze.cn)⭐⭐⭐⭐
💰 Financial AdvisorAI finance tools, Zhima OPC toolbox⭐⭐⭐⭐

The insight here isn’t the tools themselves — it’s the orchestration. The most successful OPCs aren’t the ones with the best tools. They’re the ones with the best workflows connecting them.

🏆 5 Verified OPC Success Cases

Case 1: Skincare Customer Service System — ¥3M/year

An entrepreneur built an AI-powered skincare consultation system. AI handles customer inquiries 24/7. Annual revenue: ¥3 million. Core insight: replace human customer service costs with AI, keep the margins.

Case 2: AI-Generated E-Commerce Model Photos

A designer built a business generating e-commerce product photos using AI — no actual photography needed. Fully automated revenue stream.

Case 3: 30-Person AI Coding Tool Startup — $100M/year

A team of just 30 people built an AI coding assistant that generates $100 million in annual revenue. A powerful counter-example to “you need hundreds of people.”

Case 4: Coze Agent Development

Developer DangJin built translation workflow automation agents on the Coze (Kouzi) platform, automating what was previously a tedious manual process. Multiple popular agents launched.

Case 5: From Zero to ¥35K/month

A solo entrepreneur went from zero to ¥35,000 monthly income by learning and applying AI tools for market analysis, content generation, and customer management. His formula: AI OPC = AIP × Value × AI Agent.

🏛️ Policy Roundup

National / Provincial Level

  • Guangdong: 100 OPC communities by 2028, computing subsidies, cross-border support
  • Zhejiang: OPC consortium formed, group standards in development
  • Shenzhen: 10+ communities, 1,000+ enterprises, 10,000+ talents by 2027
  • Suzhou (Wujiang): ¥2B fund, ¥10B credit, free Agent deployment, housing subsidies

Platform-Level Support

  • Zhima Enterprise Credit: OPC toolbox with AI business matching, credit building
  • WAIC × OpenCSG: Global OPC Pioneer Challenge
  • OPCBASE: Policy interpretation, community matching, resource connection
  • Suanli Xiaocang (suanlibox.com): One-stop AI service platform, API transit

🔮 Looking Ahead: Key Trends

  1. OPC Standardization Accelerates — Group standards from Zhejiang will formalize registration, operations, and compliance
  2. AI Agent Ecology Explodes — Multi-agent orchestration becomes the OPC default, up from single-tool usage
  3. OPC Community Scaling — Shenzhen, Suzhou, Hangzhou communities move from plan to physical space
  4. Traditional Organizations Reshape — OPC model forces enterprises toward distributed, AI-augmented org structures
  5. Super-Individual Branding — Personal brand becomes the primary competitive moat for OPC entrepreneurs

The Real Challenges

  • Mindset, not technology: Shifting from “employee thinking” to “CEO thinking” is harder than learning AI tools
  • Tool chain integration: Choosing the right stack and connecting it into an efficient workflow
  • Compliance: Tax, contracts, IP — different rules for one-person companies vs. traditional entities
  • The loneliness problem: Self-discipline, burnout prevention, and community support matter more than you think

🧠 Lao Qin’s Take

“2026 is OPC’s Year Zero. Tech is ready. Policy is ready. The market is ready. The only question left: are you?”

I’ve seen enough cycles to know when a window is truly open. This isn’t hype — it’s structural. Three forces (tech maturity × policy support × market validation) are converging simultaneously. That triple-whammy doesn’t come around often.

My advice for this week: Pick one vertical. Build your MVP on a low-code platform. Don’t chase perfection — chase your first paying customer. Everything else follows.

⚠️ Remember: Start small, validate fast, and for heaven’s sake — don’t YOLO your savings into this. Test as a side project first. The opportunities will still be here in 3 months.

entry.title: OPC Goes Institutional: Policy Push, 6 Proven Monetization Paths — W25 Report
entry.content:
Week 25 (June 18 – 24, 2026) — This week marked a turning point: Guangdong became China’s first province to release a dedicated AI OPC action plan, WAIC announced a global OPC startup competition, and at least six clear monetization paths have now been proven in the wild. The OPC movement is no longer a fringe concept — it’s receiving institutional backing at unprecedented speed.

🔥 Top Stories This Week

🏛️ Guangdong Releases Landmark AI OPC Action Plan

Guangdong Province published the “Supporting AI OPC Innovation Development Action Plan (2026-2028)” — the first provincial-level OPC-specific policy document in China. The targets are ambitious: 100 OPC ecological communities by 2028, nurturing 1,000 benchmark enterprises and aggregating 10,000 AI entrepreneurship talents. Computing subsidies, physical space support, financing channels, and talent programs are all on the table — a full-stack policy package.

What this means: Provincial backing signals that OPC has moved from grassroots experimentation to formal economic strategy. If you’ve been waiting for a sign to start, this is it.

🌐 WAIC 2026 Launches First-Ever OPC Track

The World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) partnered with OpenCSG to launch the “OPC Independent Pioneer Challenge” — the world’s first top-tier competition dedicated to super-individual AI entrepreneurs. The finals will be held at the WAIC 2026 venue in Shanghai’s Expo Center this July. Data cited by the organizers shows that over 1/3 of new companies are now solo-founded, with a 53% increase in the solo-founder share over 6 years.

The core logic driving this: “Carbon-based wisdom (human) + Silicon-based execution (AI) = A complete company.”

💰 City-Level Incentive Battle Heats Up

CityKey IncentiveIntensity
ShenzhenUp to ¥1M startup grant, ¥10M computing voucher⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Suzhou (Wujiang)¥50-100K startup fund, 3-year rent-free⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
ShanghaiFree office + housing at Lingang, ¥2M computing voucher⭐⭐⭐⭐
BeijingR&D subsidies ¥100-500K, priority AI talent hukou⭐⭐⭐
ZhejiangIndustry integration subsidies, low-carbon certification⭐⭐⭐

🛠️ Domestic LLMs Make AI Accessible to Everyone

China’s domestic large language models are advancing rapidly, with DeepSeek and others driving down inference costs while approaching global frontier performance. The “tech democratization” effect is real: content creation efficiency has transformed, customer service capabilities have jumped exponentially, and data analysis support is now accessible to solo founders who previously couldn’t afford such tools.

💵 6 Proven Monetization Paths (Backed by Real Cases)

Path 1: The “Shovel Seller” — AI Tool Deployment

Help non-technical individuals and SMBs set up AI environments, deploy agents, and configure workflows.

Revenue model: ¥100–500 per deployment session
Monthly ceiling: ¥10,000+ (part-time)
Real case: A 27-year-old in Wuhan taught clients how to “raise a digital lobster” (set up AI digital employees) and cashed in ¥100,000 in one week. Weekend programmers picking up OpenClaw deployment gigs routinely hit five-figure monthly income.

Path 2: The “Super Individual” — AI Replaces an Entire Team

One person + multi-agent workflow = what used to require a team of dozens.

Revenue model: Content monetization, brand deals, annual retainers
Real case: Huang Tao in Zhengzhou spent one hour training an AI assistant named “Tomato” and now runs 7 WeChat public accounts single-handedly. Topic selection, writing, formatting, contracts — all AI-managed. One article landed a ¥500,000 annual partnership.

Path 3: Custom Agent Development for SMBs

Build customer service agents, sales assistants, content tools, and data processing pipelines for small businesses.

Revenue model: ¥5,000–50,000 per project + SaaS subscriptions
Scalability: One person can manage 50+ AI digital employees simultaneously

Path 4: AI Content Entrepreneurship + Multi-Platform Distribution

Automate topic selection, writing, editing, and publishing across platforms.

Efficiency gain: 5x content output increase
Market signal: AI-related job postings are up 12x YoY, with average monthly salaries exceeding ¥60,000

Path 5: AI Music / Copyright Monetization

A niche but fast-growing segment. A Shenzhen-based post-90s creator using AI to compose music has already earned five-figure royalties.

Path 6: Vertical SaaS One-Person Unicorn

Deep industry expertise + AI coding tools = no need for large engineering teams. Founder focuses on strategy while AI handles execution.

⚡ Tech Trends Reshaping OPC

Multi-Agent Architecture Goes Mainstream

Gartner predicts 70% of enterprise AI applications will adopt multi-agent architectures by 2026. The shift is from “tuning models” to “designing agent collaboration flows” — agents autonomously divide tasks and coordinate decisions.

Desktop AI Agents Arrive

Laiye Technology launched Laiye Worker, a desktop agent product, along with an “AI Employee Family Bucket” covering finance, HR, marketing, and customer service. AI agents are moving from tech validation to actual enterprise job positions.

Native Multimodal: AI Understands the World

Models like GPT-4o, Sora 2, and Meta Muse Spark process text, images, audio, video, and 3D simultaneously from the architecture level up. One-person companies can now create rich multimedia content that previously required a full creative team.

🧠 Lao Qin’s Take

“The OPC playbook for 2026 is clear — it’s not about who has the deepest tech. It’s about who can close a commercial loop first using AI.”

Two entry paths stand out:

  • For quick cash: Be a “shovel seller” — deploy AI tools for people who can’t do it themselves. Lowest barrier, fastest validation.
  • For the long game: Become a “super individual” — train AI to be your digital twin and scale your output by 10x.

Whichever path you choose, one rule applies: Don’t YOLO into it. Validate the smallest unit of your business first, then scale.

⚠️ Risk check: Policy rollout timelines vary by region. AI tools evolve fast — expect ongoing learning investment. One-person companies have limited risk-bearing capacity — test as a side hustle before going full-time. And never ignore compliance (data privacy, IP rights).
